summary: Close the missing frontend-to-Tauri contract layer in the desktop stack by extracting explicit transport contracts and a small shared schema surface out of the monolithic desktop API client, while leaving gateway behavior and sidecar packaging unchanged.

tasks.title: Extract desktop transport contract from the monolithic API client
tasks.description: Split 4 Tauri command names `[get_gateway_base, set_gateway_base_override, check_backend_health, call_api]`, 1 request envelope `[endpoint, method, body]`, and 1 runtime-base resolution path out of `desktop/src/api/client.ts` into a dedicated desktop transport contract layer so the frontend-to-host seam stops living as inline literals and ad hoc helpers.
tasks.scope: Refactor the frontend-to-Tauri transport boundary only: introduce 2-3 desktop-side files for command names, request/response envelopes, and transport helpers; trim `desktop/src/api/client.ts` down so it consumes the extracted transport layer; keep Rust command names and runtime behavior stable in `desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`.

criteria: `desktop/src/api/client.ts` no longer owns the 4 Tauri command-name literals or the generic invoke/fetch transport envelope.
1 desktop transport contract layer exists and is the single source for `[command names, HTTP method type, request envelope, base normalization/runtime base helpers]`.
`desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` still exposes the same 4 commands and matches the extracted contract naming without adding new runtime branches.
convergence.verification: npm --prefix desktop run typecheck && npm --prefix desktop run test -- src/api/client.test.ts && cargo check --manifest-path desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml
convergence.definition_of_done: The desktop frontend-to-host transport seam is explicit, importable, and behavior-preserving, and future client work can depend on the extracted transport layer instead of editing inline Tauri literals in `client.ts`.

implementation.title: Inventory the current transport seam
implementation.description: Map the current base-resolution helpers, cached runtime-base logic, generic `callApi` bridge, and the 4 Tauri command usages inside `desktop/src/api/client.ts` and `desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`.

implementation.title: Create the desktop transport contract layer
implementation.description: Extract shared command constants, request-envelope types, and transport helpers into dedicated desktop API files, then update `client.ts` to consume them instead of defining them inline.

implementation.title: Align the Rust host with the extracted contract
implementation.description: Keep `main.rs` command registration behavior unchanged while aligning its command documentation and handler signatures with the extracted desktop transport contract so the seam is explicit on both sides.

tasks.title: Extract cross-cutting desktop gateway schemas and thin the endpoint facade
tasks.description: Move 3 cross-cutting schema families `[GatewayHealth/runtime, GatewayServiceConfig admin, WritingHelper request-response]` out of `desktop/src/api/client.ts` into a desktop-side shared schema layer, then keep `client.ts` as a thin facade that reuses the extracted transport contract and shared DTO exports.
tasks.scope: Refactor shared desktop schema ownership only: extract reused DTOs and response wrappers from `client.ts`, update `client.test.ts` to validate the split, and leave endpoint behavior, route inventory, and gateway payload semantics unchanged.

criteria: The 3 shared schema families `[GatewayHealth/runtime, GatewayServiceConfig admin, WritingHelper request-response]` live outside `desktop/src/api/client.ts` and are imported from 1 desktop-side schema file or folder.
`desktop/src/api/client.ts` remains the public endpoint facade, but its inline type surface is reduced to endpoint-local types instead of transport and shared contracts.
`desktop/src/api/client.test.ts` or successor focused tests cover the extracted transport/schema split without reducing existing desktop API regression coverage.
convergence.verification: npm --prefix desktop run typecheck && npm --prefix desktop run test -- src/api/client.test.ts
convergence.definition_of_done: Cross-cutting desktop API schemas are owned by an explicit shared contract layer, `client.ts` is materially smaller and transport-agnostic, and the split is locked by desktop tests.

implementation.title: Select the shared schema families
implementation.description: Identify the reused DTO groups in `client.ts` that cross multiple panels, tests, or runtime helpers, starting with gateway health/runtime, service config admin, and writing-helper request/response types.

implementation.title: Extract the shared contract file
implementation.description: Move the selected DTO families into a dedicated desktop schema file or folder and update `client.ts` exports so current callers can keep importing through stable paths.

implementation.title: Rebaseline desktop API tests
implementation.description: Update `client.test.ts` to validate the new import boundaries and preserve regression coverage for base resolution, transport fallback, and representative shared-schema endpoints.

cross_module_dependencies.reason: Module A is expected to tighten authoritative gateway integration boundaries; C2 should extract desktop shared schemas after those backend payload/unsupported-shape decisions settle so the new desktop contract layer does not freeze transitional gateway shapes.

risks: `desktop/src/api/client.ts` currently mixes transport logic with a very large inline DTO surface, so trying to move every type in one pass would expand the module beyond a follow-up queue item.

`desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` currently marshals the transport seam as `String` and `Option<String>` payloads, so the split must preserve command names and wire format instead of introducing a new host protocol.

Existing desktop tests are concentrated in `desktop/src/api/client.test.ts`, so the split needs explicit regression coverage or the contract extraction will look structurally clean while reducing confidence.
out_of_scope: Changing gateway endpoint behavior or payload semantics in `src-ts`.
Reworking sidecar runtime selection, externalBin packaging, or `desktop/scripts/validate_sidecar_contract.cjs`.
Adding new desktop features, new API routes, or new user-facing flows.
